Variants.Content: Mance Rayder's following is an alliance forged from many clans of the free folk. Mance once wore the black cloak of the Night's Watch before crossing back beyond the Wall to live among the free folk; relying on song, wide knowledge, persuasion, and necessary duels, he made feuding clans acknowledge a single direction. The free folk refuse to kneel, so his 'kingship' is not granted by a southern throne, but is a following that must be continually earned. Mance's true strength lies in making people understand that when a colder, older threat draws near, if old blood feuds are not set aside for the moment, every clan will be swallowed by the snow.

The free folk follow Mance not because he has royal blood, but because he has walked among their campfires, understands their quarrels, and can defeat those who refuse to listen to reason. If he cannot keep proving himself, no title can bind a people who do not kneel.

The Night's Watch regards Mance as the most dangerous kind of deserter, because he understands both the castles and ways of the black brothers and why the free folk are moving south. Some see only oathbreaking, while others are forced to admit that he has gathered together peoples who had not truly united in hundreds of years.

People south of the Wall often call everyone under Rayder 'wildlings,' as though they had neither names nor fears. Northern border folk know better that within that tide of people are warriors, and also families clutching their children, wanting only to flee the cold and death.

Entry Reed The Rayder faction forms around Mance Rayder, the King-Beyond-the-Wall, who temporarily unites the clans of the free folk through persuasion, single combat, and shared crisis. The family crest is just a facade, the real weight of the family is whether they can protect their fiefdom, honor their engagements, and rally people in times of crisis.
